findings.summary: Termination condition 3 ignores the spec's explicit qualifier that it must not end the run while work is outstanding. Spec §3 line 37 states in bold: 「条件 3 只拦新 clue，已 open 的跑完」—— the depth cap blocks new clues while already-open clues run to completion. decideTermination instead returns a non-null terminal state ('capped') the instant max(depth) >= cfg.maxDepth, with no in_flight / open / proposed guard, and the doc comment at src/tick.ts:167 fixes the contract that a non-null state means terminated. So the moment any depth-maxDepth clue appears on the board, the run is declared over and every in-flight worker's and open clue's work is abandoned — the opposite of 「已 open 的跑完」. Contrast condition 1 at src/tick.ts:206-210, which does gate on inFlight === 0 && proposed === 0; condition 3 was given no equivalent drain gate. The TerminationState type also has no way to express 'capped but still draining', so the qualifier is unimplemented at the API level, not merely at the branch level. Both coherent readings of line 37 (cap applies at clue creation, or cap fires once the frontier reaches maxDepth) require the run to drain before reporting capped, so the divergence stands either way. Note this errs in the unsafe direction — it truncates research early — unlike the conservative under-dispatch noted in the S2 final review.

The capped branch takes unconditional precedence over the blocked downgrade, so a run with blocked > 0 that also trips condition 2 or 3 reports 'capped' rather than 'partial'. Spec §3.2 is marked ⛔ and reads 「blocked > 0 时终态一律不得为『正常收敛』/ 只能是『部分完成』」—— literally, blocked > 0 admits only partial. The safety core of §3.2 does hold (state === 'converged' is reachable only through the else-branch where blocked === 0, so no falsely-complete report is ever emitted, and capped likewise disclaims completeness), which is why this is not a blocker. But the blocked degradation is silently absorbed into the cap verdict, and no test covers the blocked+capped overlap: C8 and C9 (test/s3.test.ts:129-154) both construct scenarios well under maxClues and maxDepth, so neither exercises the precedence.

C7's assertion cannot discriminate the condition-3 defect above. The case supplies a single card with default status 'explored', so in_flight, open and proposed are all 0 — a drain-aware implementation of condition 3 would return 'capped' for exactly this input too. The mechanical acceptance row is therefore satisfied by both the delivered behavior and the spec-faithful behavior, which is why the §8 mutation table has no entry that would have caught it. A discriminating case would hold one card at depth >= maxDepth alongside an in_flight or open card and assert the run has not yet terminated.

runTick never calls decideTermination or computeCoverage, and TickDeps/BoardState carry no evidence-reading affordance, so the delivered scheduler tick still does not perform spec §3.2 steps 5-6 at runtime; the new logic is reachable only from future S4 code. I treat this as informational rather than a defect: this package's termination decision has no side effect of its own to perform (halting the loop is loop-engine wiring, deferred by §9), threading it through runTick would have required changing runTick's existing exported return type in violation of §9's frozen-signature rule, and none of C1-C15 exercises a shell. Flagging it because §1 describes the deliverable as 「调度器 tick 的后半段」, and the tick as delivered does not yet contain it.

The TickConfig field comment still reads 「最大深度（本包只透传，不消费）」, which was accurate under S2 but is now false: decideTermination consumes cfg.maxDepth as termination condition 3 at src/tick.ts:201. Stale comment only, no behavioral effect.

Spec §8 requires per-assertion attribution of the P1-P6 mutation self-check, and §7 requires demonstrating the tightened B1 guard actually bites by temporarily injecting Date.now() into the checked source. No tracked file in the subject tree carries either record — there is no IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY, and my read-only file inspection cannot read commit message bodies, so I can neither confirm nor refute that the evidence was recorded there. I verified the attribution mechanically instead: P1 dies on C1 (test/s3.test.ts:35-37, set size 1 vs length 5); P2 dies on C3 (:52-58, prevZeroGrowthRounds 1 -> 0 on growth); P3 dies on C5a (:77-86, which is non-degenerate — its inputs reach zeroGrowthRounds 2 with proposed 0, so dropping the in-flight sub-condition would yield 'converged' against an asserted null); P4 dies on C6 (:113-119); P5 dies on both C8 and C9 (:129-154), the package's core judgment. C3 and C11 both satisfy the §8.1 stubbing discipline: their paired calls differ in exactly the asserted dimension and assert the delta/ordering (:190, t2 === t1 + 1) rather than two absolute values. P6 is the exception — reverting the guard regex to /new\s+Date/ is killed by no committed test, since src/tick.ts contains none of the three forbidden tokens; only the §7 injection run could have demonstrated it, and that run left no trace.

The only committed acceptance evidence belongs to a different development: this file carries development_id dev_ledr_s2_tick_01 and a run of 42 tests across protocol/tick/cas/bus that predates test/s3.test.ts, so it does not evidence C14 (npm run typecheck and npm test exit 0) for this package. Informational only — the acceptance stage regenerates it, and my static review found nothing that would fail either command: tsconfig.json is strict with include [src, test], and test/s3.test.ts type-checks (TerminalState, BoardCard and TickConfig are all exported, the non-null assertions at :170 narrow TerminalState | null correctly, and every decideTermination literal supplies all four TerminationInput fields). C15 also holds — the pre-existing suites still carry exactly 11 + 16 + 10 + 5 = 42 it( cases, with s3.test.ts adding 15 net new.
